rules.text: Build a wide candidate pool cheaply: run each base reducer (pyzx_full_reduce, tket FullPeepholeOptimise, pyzx_teleport_reduce, pyzx_clifford_simp) both on the lowered circuit AND cross-applied to each other's output (e.g. pyzx_full_reduce(tket(...))) before folding; cross terms often beat either alone.

Always pair every reducer output with tools.fold_resynth(tools.canonicalize(x)) as a separate candidate rather than only folding the single current best; phase folding gains are not monotonic across reducers so folding only the winner misses cheaper folded alternatives.

Gate each successive tools.block_optimize stage on tools.time_left() with strictly decreasing thresholds (e.g. 40,25,15,10) and always re-seed from tools.best(candidates) so far, not from a fixed variable, to avoid wasting budget refining an already-dominated candidate.

More candidate branches is not free: each extra tools.pyzx_full_reduce/fold_resynth/block_optimize call burns charged CPU time and risks pushing past budget, which can cost more than it gains. Before adding a new candidate source, check it beats an existing one on at least one real benchmark, not just 'more diversity'.

When adding block_optimize stages, raise thresholds as you add more stages (e.g. 50,35,20) rather than reusing the previous program's thresholds unchanged; extra stages inserted before existing ones shift effective time budgets and can starve the final stages, hurting score even when each stage individually looks sound.

Diffs must contain the exact parent text verbatim for the SEARCH block to match (whitespace, line breaks, docstring included) — do not paraphrase or drop the docstring/comments when quoting the parent snippet, or the edit is rejected as unparseable.

When emitting a SEARCH/REPLACE diff, the SEARCH block must match the parent program's text byte-for-byte exactly once (same whitespace, blank lines, comments). Prefer rewriting the whole function body as one SEARCH block (e.g. the full 'def optimize(...):...return ...' text) rather than a small fragment, since partial-line fragments are the usual cause of 'found 0 times' failures.

Every branch added inside a tools.time_left() gate must still update `best` with tools.best(candidates) AND the function must end with an unconditional `return best` (or equivalent) after all gates. A program that appends candidates but falls through without a final return, or returns early inside a gate, produces no score even if individual stages are sound.

Before adding a 4th/5th raw candidate source (teleport_reduce, extra fold_resynth passes, etc.), verify each adds distinct value: fold_resynth on near-identical inputs (e.g. fold_resynth(a) and fold_resynth(lowered) when a already dominates lowered) rarely changes the winner and just burns CPU time charged against the tie-break.

If unsure, make the SEARCH block the entire parent file text and the REPLACE block the entire new file text.

rules.text: Each candidate added via tools.block_optimize should be built by re-canonicalizing the CURRENT best (tools.canonicalize(best)) at the point of the call, not a stale candidate captured earlier in the function; stale inputs to later stages silently waste budget on an already-dominated circuit even when thresholds are correctly staggered per R3/R5.

When adding a new pyzx/tket reduction variant (e.g. pyzx_clifford_simp, pyzx_teleport_reduce) feeding into fold_resynth, append both the raw and folded result to candidates before calling tools.best, so a stage that folds poorly doesn't discard a raw reduction that was already better than the prior best.

Before emitting a SEARCH/REPLACE diff, count occurrences of the exact SEARCH string in the shown parent text yourself (mentally scan start-to-end once); if it is not exactly 1, widen the SEARCH block (add surrounding lines) or switch to whole-file SEARCH/REPLACE rather than submitting a guessed fragment.

Before emitting a diff, copy the SEARCH block directly from the parent text shown in THIS turn (not memory, not a prior accepted diff's summary), including the leading docstring, blank lines, and exact indentation. Default to making SEARCH the entire parent file and REPLACE the entire new file unless the change is a single isolated line.

R16 [candidate] Chained block_optimize stages each cost real wall-time beyond tools.time_left() budget checks (block_size/max_gates scale cost). If adding a new gated stage, also shrink max_gates or block_size on later stages, or add a tools.time_left() margin (e.g. require >2x the stage's typical cost) to avoid wall-time-limit verifier failures on large circuits like qpe_8.

R18 [candidate] When a program already has 5+ staged tools.block_optimize calls, prefer editing thresholds/adding candidates to tools.best rather than appending yet another stage; each extra stage increases wall-time risk on large benchmarks without proportionally improving the geometric-mean score.
